today.expert: 8 golds, 3–5 traps, 75 % look-alikes, gold up 1 s

measured: Elite held to human limits 124 / 114 / 106 / 100 (Expert best tenth 123); 140 ms elite 188 / 186 / 187 / 183 (speed-levels-tune, 100 deals). Average player: not documented.

hard: 8 golds; 3–5 traps before each (about 32 a round against Normal's 13), each 0.45 s long and 0.6–1 s apart, the first inside the first second; 75 % gold look-alikes; gold up 0.9 s.

glance.easy: A calm dark glass; the first gold arrives within three seconds.
glance.hard: Trap colours fire about once a second from the start.
glance.expert: The glass flickers twice a second, nearly all gold look-alikes.

why: The only thing Flash can ask beyond a fast finger is not to be fooled, so the traps multiply and quicken while the gold's own window never drops below 0.6 s, more than twice the 0.25 s limit.
proof: Open by design (a reaction game). At 0.25 s a gold pays 115 on tapRev 7's curve, so with the 15-point steady hand the limits player tops out at 130 on every level, Normal included. Expert's 200 needs I1's tapRev 8 with the curve's full mark at 250 ms (I1 as written, 250 ms = 150, still caps the limits player at 165). With that, playFlashHuman in scripts/speed-levels-tune.ts must reach 200 in its best tenth at Expert, pinned in scripts/speed-levels-check.ts.
stamp: Level field only: the deal stamps flashMs (as today) and a new trapMs that the stage and replayFlash read. Expert's 200 also needs I1's tapRev 8 (Joe's scoring decision).
risk: Until I1 moves the curve no level can pass 130 under the limits, and fast full-screen flashes must stay under three a second.
